ApiLanguage.description: The REST API server language. GO (the default) emits the chi server module, RUST the axum crate, TYPESCRIPT the Hono package built on the TypeScript HTTP runtime (`<out>/api/<service>`, `<scope>/<service>-api`).

ApiOutputConfig.description: The REST API server. The server imports the service's types in its language, so an enabled API needs that language enabled in types: go for GO (the default), rust for RUST, typescript for TYPESCRIPT.

mcp.description: Serve the operations the mcp decorator makes visible tools over MCP at POST /api/mcp (D81): the caller authenticates as on the API's other routes, and each tools/call runs through the route of its operation. A TypeScript, a Rust and a Go API serve it (#660). Unset is off.

mcpConfirmationKey.description: The Secret<string> config field the MCP endpoint signs the confirmations of its ask tools with (D93), by the envVars class that declares it and the field's name, as a stack names the secret: "McpKeys.MCP_CONFIRMATION_KEY". The API's envVars class holds the field, its own or one it extends; its value is a random string of at least 32 bytes, one per environment. Required with mcp when a visible tool's invocation policy is ask.

CiOutputConfig.description: The CI a Stack service's build writes, keyed by the renderer that writes it: github for GitHub Actions, or a renderer an extension registers. Only a Stack service sets it. The build writes each workflow under <out>/ci/<stack>/.

CiRendererConfig.description: One CI renderer's options for a Stack service's generated workflow.

branch.description: The branch pull requests target and a push deploys from: a branch name, not a pattern. Unset is "main".

install.description: The directory, relative to the repository root, the build installs the workflow into when it exists. Unset is the renderer's own, .github/workflows for github.

ExtensionKind.description: The name of a kind an extension registers ("Catalog"). The authoring packages cannot see the registry, so the name is any string here; superschematic checks it against the registered kinds when it loads the config.

SchemaConfigDocument.description:
The schema.config.json / schema.config.yaml document shape.

This is the SchemaConfig contract projected onto plain data: authDb is the service name, and dependencies and calls are explicit arrays of name + kind pairs (there is no import system in the JSON/YAML forms to derive them from). superschematic validates the data forms against the JSON Schema generated from this type (see the gen-json-schema package script).

buckets.description: The Bucket services this API's implementation uses: each is a Bucket in its Deps, and a bucket edge from its server and jobs. Only an API service sets it, and each entry names a Bucket service.

calls.description: The API services this API's implementation calls, or this site's code calls from the browser. Only an API or a Site service sets it, and each entry names an API service. Each callee is built before its caller.

clientVersions.description: Whether this API turns away a client too old to speak to it. With true its EnvConfig gains an optional setting, MIN_CLIENT_VERSIONS, a list such as "cli=0.5.0,desktop=2.1.0", and a request whose X-Client-Version header names a listed client at a lower version is answered 426 with the problem client_too_old. Only an API service sets it.

contentAddressed.description: Whether this Bucket service names its objects by their content. With true, an API that lists it gets a content bucket in its Deps: put reads a body whole, names the object sha256/<hex> by the SHA-256 of its bytes and writes it if absent, and has, missing, get and signedUrl read by hash. Only a Bucket service sets it.

maxBytes.description: The largest object a content-addressed bucket puts, in bytes: a whole number above 0, 33554432 (32 MiB) when absent. Only a Bucket service whose contentAddressed is true sets it.

memoryStores.description: The MemoryStore services this API's implementation uses: each is a MemoryStore in its Deps, and a memoryStore edge from its server, jobs and workers. Only an API service sets it, and each entry names a MemoryStore service.

outputs.description: The generated outputs. A Site service has none, and may leave it out.

providers.description: The runtime provider packages this API may use (D159): each its directory, relative to the service's directory and starting with "./" or "../", or its npm name ("@scope/name" or "name"), which resolves from the node_modules of the service's directory or one above it (#608). The package's package.json declares the provider under "superschematic": { "provider": ... }. The build reads each and checks it against its interface's contract, and the provider slots of the API's envVars class name one of them per environment. Only an API service sets it.

rateLimitStore.description: The MemoryStore service this API's rate-limited routes count in, so its replicas share one budget per client; while the store is unavailable each replica counts in process. It is listed in memoryStores whether or not that list names it. Only an API service sets it.

site.description: How a Site service builds and what it serves. Only a Site service sets it.

SchemaKind.description: The kinds the core compiler registers. Closed: an extension adds a kind by registering it with superschematic, not by extending this enum. A Stack service declares what runs where over the others (`@superschematic/stack`) and is named by none, so it has no sentinel. A Site service is a static site: its config names the APIs it calls and how it builds, and its code sits at its implementation path (D55). A Bucket service is private object storage that APIs list in their `buckets` (D54): its config is all it has, `{ name, kind: SchemaKind.Bucket, outputs: {} }`, with `contentAddressed: true` for one that names its objects by their content (D142). A MemoryStore service is a Redis or Valkey server the replicas of a stack share, which holds no fact (D75): its schema declares each channel and key it carries (`@superschematic/memory-store`), and APIs list it in their `memoryStores`. A Tasks service declares the work a commit of its repository needs, a class per task (`@superschematic/tasks`, D203): its build writes the task file a forge reads, and nothing names it, so it has no sentinel.

SchemaKindName.description: What a config's `kind` admits: a core SchemaKind member or an extension kind name.

SchemaOutputsDocument.description: The outputs block of the data forms: the core keys, plus the output key of any generator an extension registers. The authoring packages cannot see the registry, so an extension key is any name here; superschematic checks each key against the registered generators, and each section against its generator's OutputSchema, when it reads the config.

SdkOutputConfig.description: The client SDK in each language. An SDK imports the service's types in its language, so each enabled SDK language needs the same language enabled in types.

ServiceDependencyRef.description: A service reference in the JSON/YAML config forms, in dependencies, calls, buckets, memoryStores and rateLimitStore. The TypeScript form builds ServiceHandle sentinels with the service() helper; the data forms carry the same name + kind pair as a plain object.

SiteConfig.description: How a Site service builds and what it serves (D55). Its code is the package at the naming file's [implementation_paths] site template, web/{service} unless set, a member of the Bun workspace.

build.description: The script of the site's package.json that builds it, which a deploy runs with bun run after a frozen install of the workspace. Unset is "build".

dev.description: The site's dev server, which stack dev runs in place of building the site once, behind a proxy that serves the site and each API it calls on one origin (D82). A deploy builds the site whether it is set or not. Unset, stack dev builds the site once.

fallback.description: The file, relative to output, served for a path that names no file: "index.html" for a single-page application, whose router reads the path. Unset answers such a path 404.

output.description: The directory the build writes, relative to the site's directory and inside it. Unset is "dist".

SiteDevConfig.description: How a site's dev server runs under stack dev (D82): Vite, Bun's own (bun ./index.html), or any server that serves the site's code and reloads it on an edit.

command.description: The script of the site's package.json, or a binary of its dependencies, that runs the dev server, which stack dev runs with bun run after the workspace's install. Arguments go in the script. Unset is "dev".

port.description: The port the dev server listens on, on loopback, for a command that picks its own. Unset, stack dev picks a port per checkout and hands it to the command in PORT, which the script passes on: "vite --port $PORT --strictPort".

SqlDialect.description: A database the DB kind's sql output is built for.

SqlEncryptionConfig.description: The keys of a DB service's Encrypted<T> fields (D85).

key.description: The Secret<string> field of an env vars class that holds the keys, by the type that declares the field and the field's name, as a stack names the secret: "FieldKeys.FINANCES_DB_KEY". Its value is one or more 32-byte keys in base64, separated by commas; the first encrypts, and each decrypts what it encrypted. Every API whose servers, jobs and workers open the service's ORM must hold the field in its env vars class.

SqlOutputConfig.description: The DB kind's sql output. The DDL and the ORM are implied by the kind; this block places and owns the generated projection view migrations and lists the dialects the DDL is written for.

dialects.description: The databases the service is built for. With sqlite listed, the build also writes sqlite/create.sql and refuses a schema that uses what SQLite does not support, and migrate plan --dialect sqlite plans for it. The list must hold postgres: the Go ORM the kind always generates runs on Postgres. Unset is ["postgres"].

encryption.description: Where the keys of the schema's Encrypted<T> fields come from (D85). A schema with one needs it.

migrationsDir.description: Where the projection view migrations are written, relative to the service directory. Unset keeps them under <out>/sql/<service>/projections/migrations.

requireUpdatedBy.description: An update of a table with an updatedBy field needs an acting user, as a create of a table with createdBy does: without one the ORMs refuse it (NoUserError in TypeScript, ErrNoUserInContext in Go) where they would leave a nullable updatedBy as it was (D87). Unset is false.

search.description: The database's search index (#740): how the words of its

sourceSchema.description: The Postgres schema that holds the tables the views read: each view selects <sourceSchema>.<table> for its source table and every joined table, so it does not depend on the migration runner's search_path. Unset leaves the tables unqualified.

systemActor.description: Who the ORMs act as for a write no request's caller makes, a job's or a worker's: orm.asSystem() in TypeScript and orm.AsSystem(ctx) in Go stamp createdBy, updatedBy and deletedBy with its id (D87). The audit fields hold a user's id with no foreign key, so it needs no user row. Unset is { id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000", name: "system" }.

viewOwner.description: The Postgres role the migrations create the views as: SET ROLE around the view DDL and RESET ROLE after it, so the schema's default privileges for that role apply. The migration runner must be a member of the role. Unset creates the views as the runner.

SqlSearchConfig.description: The search index of a DB service (D155, #740).

environment.description: Search the database's @searchable tables through its environment's search index, which the stack's search database holds (@stack({ search }), #740): its worker copies each index row there after its commit, its tables' triggers enqueue every write of a row and its grants table's every write of a grant. Postgres alone. Unset is false.

environmentIndex.description: Hold the environment's search index, environment_search_index, a copy of the index rows of the environment's databases that a stack names this database for (@stack({ search }), #740). Postgres alone. Unset is false.

foldDiacritics.description: Fold diacritics, so a word finds its accented forms: on Postgres the index's words and a search's query go through the unaccent dictionary (the migrations make a text search configuration, search_unaccent, and the unaccent extension where the database lacks it), and on SQLite the FTS5 table removes diacritics. Turning it on or off migrates the index: its GIN index is built again on Postgres, and its FTS5 table on SQLite. Unset is false.

SqlSystemActorConfig.description: The system actor of a DB service's ORMs (D87).

id.description: The actor's user id: a UUID, hyphenated.

name.description: The name an app shows for the actor. Unset is "system".

TasksCiOutputConfig.description: The CI renderers of a Tasks service, by name.

TasksCiRendererConfig.description: One CI renderer of a Tasks service.

install.description: The directory the workflow is committed in, from the repository root. Its default is the renderer's own, .github/workflows for github. It must exist.

TasksOutputConfig.description: The task file a Tasks service's build writes, and the workflow of each CI its tasks run on. Only a Tasks service sets it. The build writes the files under <out>/tasks/<service>/.

ci.description: The CI the tasks run on, keyed by the renderer that writes its workflow: github for GitHub Actions, which reads the github section of the task file, or a renderer an extension registers. Each task is a job. Every build-all installs the workflow, and tasks --check holds it current as it holds the task file.

install.description: The path the task file is committed at, from the repository root, as ci/tasks.json. Its directory must exist. Every build-all installs the file there, and tasks --check fails when the committed file is not what the schema gives. Unset, the file is written under the output root alone.

TypeScriptSdkOutputConfig.description: The TypeScript SDK. With lazyValidation, the SDK loads its types package's validators and parsers, and with them superscalar's WebAssembly core, on its first call rather than when it is imported (D82): a browser bundle that splits code (Vite, bun build --splitting) carries them in a chunk of its own, out of the page's first load.

TypesOutputConfig.description: The type library in each language. A library imports the types of every dependency it takes types from, so each such dependency must enable the same languages; build-all and build --with-deps refuse a build where one does not. A DB schema needs go: the Go ORM the kind always generates imports the Go types.
